Additional supportive features are nonenhancement, absent enhancing component, frontal/cortical involvement, and a large T2/FLAIR-predominant tumor burden, all of which can fit an IDH-mutant diffuse glioma. Against IDH mutation, the patient is older, and the lesion is multifocal/bilateral with midline crossing, deep white matter and ependymal invasion, large volume, and mass effect, which are more concerning for aggressive IDH-wildtype biology. Overall, the T2-FLAIR mismatch and nonenhancing frontal/cortical pattern outweigh the age and infiltrative extent, so the best estimate is IDH-mutant.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structured MRI metadata without DWI/ADC, perfusion, spectroscopy, SWI/GRE, or histology. The T2-FLAIR mismatch strongly supports an IDH-mutant, non-codeleted astrocytoma phenotype, but the patient age, multifocal/bilateral extent, ependymal/deep invasion, mass effect, and reported necrosis raise concern for high-grade behavior. The nonenhancing appearance is atypical for many grade 4 tumors, so histomolecular confirmation remains essential.
